summary: Mostly not. Crossings up of a short ATR over a long one, and every setting on daily candles, did the same as random entries. The result that holds up is about quiet markets: going long while ATR(14) sat below ATR(100) did worse than random on 1h and 4h, and on 4h it holds without its strongest stretch and at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles.

verdicts.use: Going long while volatility is high (ATR(14) above ATR(100))
verdicts.text: Beat random on 1h, but on 4h only through the stretch between Jul 31 and Sep 24, 2021. These entries are volatile candles in a window that rose, so price moved more after them without picking a direction.

verdicts.use: Going long while volatility is quiet (ATR(14) below ATR(100))
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h and 4h. On 4h it shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles, and the gap comes from uptrends.

verdicts.use: Going long as volatility picks up (ATR(14) crossing up ATR(100), ATR(7) crossing up ATR(28))
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily, for both pairs of lengths.

verdicts.text: Same as random for every setting on daily candles.

notes: Going long while ATR(14) was below ATR(100) on 4h gave 23,720 entries in 237 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.39% behind random entries, below the luck band. That gap shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and holds without its strongest stretch, between Dec 8, 2021 and Jan 21, 2022. It comes from uptrends, at 0.61% behind random; in downtrends it was the same as random.

On 1h the same setting was 0.1% behind random, below the band, and it holds without its strongest stretch between Apr 7 and Apr 30, 2022. It fades by 50 candles. On 1h the trend split runs the other way: same as random in uptrends, worse in downtrends. SOL shows it at every horizon, 0.19% behind on 1h and 0.89% behind on 4h.

Going long while ATR(14) was above ATR(100) beat random by 0.13% on 1h and 0.55% on 4h, and by 1.35% on SOL 4h. These entries cluster in volatile candles in a window that rose. Price moved more after them because of when they fire, not because they pick a direction.

Neither high-ATR result covers both trends. On 1h it fades by 50 candles and was the same as random in uptrends. In 1h downtrends it rests on signals on Jan 8–17, 2023. On 4h it rests on the stretch between Jul 31 and Sep 24, 2021, and in downtrends it was the same as random.

ATR(14) crossing up through ATR(100) and ATR(7) crossing up through ATR(28) landed the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. The 1h cross down through ATR(100) looked worse than random only because of 4 entries on Feb 1–2, 2025. On 1h, ATR(7) crossing up through ATR(28) beat random on SOL and in downtrends. It also fires in volatile candles, so it shows price moving more, not a direction.

For a long DCA bot, the reading to note is quiet volatility on 4h. Entries while ATR(14) sat below ATR(100) trailed random, mostly in uptrends, which is a reason to leave that condition out of a long bot's start conditions. High-ATR entries moved more but chose no direction, so they belong beside a direction filter, with the take profit and DCA steps sized for the larger moves. The bot form compares ATR with a fixed value, so to test these ATR-versus-ATR conditions you send them in as a TradingView signal.
